item.title: 2006: Red Sox Bid $51.1 Million to Land Daisuke Matsuzaka
item.description: The Boston Red Sox file the highest bid, US$51.1 million, in the posting system and win the rights to negotiate with Seibu Lions pitcher Daisuke Matsuzaka. Matsuzaka has a gyroball among his arsenal of pitches and, while playing for champions Japan, was MVP at the 2006 World Baseball Classic. Photo: User Mori Chan on Flickr (Original version) User UCinternational (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2024: Blue Jays Hire Bell as VP of Baseball Operations, Assistant GM
item.description: On November 15, 2024, the Toronto Blue Jays hired Bell to the concurrent roles of vice president of baseball operations and assistant general manager. Photo: Ryan Casey Aguinaldo (CC BY-SA 4.0).

item.title: 2022: Brewers Add Turang to 40-Man Roster, Protect Him From Rule 5
item.description: On November 15, 2022, the Brewers added Turang to their 40–man roster to protect him from the Rule 5 draft. Photo: Sewageboy (CC BY-SA 4.0).

item.title: 2016: Cora Becomes Bench Coach for Houston Astros
item.description: On November 15, 2016, Cora became the bench coach for the Houston Astros. Photo: Keith Allison on Flickr (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2016: Bob Addis, 91, Backup Outfielder and Euclid High School Coach
item.description: Bob Addis, 91, backup outfielder for the Boston Braves, Chicago Cubs and Pittsburgh Pirates in 208 games from 1950 to 1953, who later worked as a baseball coach and athletic director at Euclid High School in Ohio, leading the team to a state championship in 1963.

item.title: 2015: Dodger Stadium Hosts Cricket All-Stars Series Finale, Led by Tendulkar
item.description: On November 15, 2015, Dodger Stadium hosted the third and final game of the Cricket All-Stars Series 2015, featuring many retired cricket players from around the world and led by great cricket legends Sachin Tendulkar and Shane Warne. Photo: Ken Lund from Reno, Nevada, USA (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2014: Salt River Rafters Beat Peoria Javelinas 14-7, Win Arizona Fall League
item.description: The Salt River Rafters outlast the Peoria Javelinas, 14–7, to win their fourth Arizona Fall League title and first since 2011. Rafters outfielder Eddie Rosario (Twins), who lost the batting title in his last at-bat of the regular season, goes 4 for 5 with a double, one home run, two runs and two RBI. The Javelinas' Justin O'Conner (Rays), who already had made a name for himself as the best defensive and…

item.title: 2005: Albert Pujols Wins First Career MVP, First Cardinal Since McGee
item.description: Albert Pujols of the St. Louis Cardinals wins his first career MVP Award, becoming the first Cardinal to win the honor since Willie McGee in 1985. Photo: shgmom56 (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 1991: Reds Trade Greg Swindell to Indians for Scudder and Two Others
item.description: On November 15, 1991, the Reds traded Scudder, Jack Armstrong, and Joe Turek to the Cleveland Indians for pitcher Greg Swindell. Photo: Grand Slam Card Company (Public domain).

item.title: 1991: Expos Reclaim Gary Carter off Waivers From Dodgers
item.description: Gary Carter returns to the Montreal Expos when they claim him off waivers from the Los Angeles Dodgers.

item.title: 1989: Bret Saberhagen, 25, Wins Second AL Cy Young With 27 of 28 Votes
item.description: Bret Saberhagen of the Kansas City Royals wins his second career AL Cy Young Award, capturing 27 of a possible 28 first-place votes. Saberhagen, 25, led the AL in victories (23), earned run average (2.16) and innings pitched (262<small>1/3</small>).

item.title: 1988: Kirk Gibson Wins NL MVP in First Season in National League
item.description: Kirk Gibson, the fiery outfielder who drove the Los Angeles Dodgers to a pennant and world championship, is elected Most Valuable Player in his first season in the National League. With 13 of 24 first-place votes and 272 points, he outdistances two members of the New York Mets, Darryl Strawberry (seven, 236) and Kevin McReynolds (four, 162).

item.title: 1982: Hal McRae, 36, Re-Signs With Royals After Free Agency
item.description: Kansas City Royals DH and team leader Hal McRae, 36, signs a new contract to remain with the club, five days after being granted free agency. McRae led the American League in runs batted in (133) in 1982 and was named to his third All-Star team.

item.title: 1980: Braves Sign Claudell Washington, Granted Free Agency by Mets
item.description: The Atlanta Braves sign outfielder Claudell Washington, granted free agency from the New York Mets on October 31.

item.title: 1972: Dick Allen Wins Landslide AL MVP With White Sox, Leads in Homers
item.description: Dick Allen of the Chicago White Sox is a landslide winner of the 1972 American League Most Valuable Player Award. An eight-year veteran of three NL teams, Allen has had a huge impact in his first year in the Junior Circuit—leading it in homers (37), runs batted in (113), bases on balls (99), OBP (.420), slugging percentage (.603), OPS (1.023), and OPS+ (.199).

item.title: 1969: Billy Southworth, 76, Hall of Fame Manager With 1,044 Wins
item.description: Billy Southworth, 76, Hall of Fame manager who won 1,044 regular-season games as skipper of the St. Louis Cardinals (1929 and 1940–1945) and Boston Braves (1946–1951); captured World Series titles in 1942 and 1944 and National League pennants with St. Louis (1943) and Boston (1948); his .597 career winning percentage is second, all-time, to Joe McCarthy; in his playing days, an outfielder who appeared in 1,192 games… Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1967: Carl Yastrzemski Wins Near-Unanimous AL MVP After Triple Crown
item.description: Capturing all but one first-place vote (and 275 points), Triple-Crown-winner Carl Yastrzemski is a near-unanimous choice for the 1967 AL Most Valuable Player Award. Minneapolis baseball writer Max Nichols' strongly criticized vote for hometown player César Tovar is the lone dissenting tally. Photo: Steven Carter from Northern New England, USA (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 1961: Roger Maris Wins Second Straight AL MVP, Edging Mickey Mantle
item.description: Roger Maris wins his second consecutive American League Most Valuable Player Award, squeaking past his teammate Mickey Mantle by four votes.

item.title: 1951: Willie Mays Wins First Major Honor, Rookie of the Year
item.description: Willie Mays, the brilliant, 20-year-old centerfielder of the New York Giants, and Gil McDougald, 23, versatile infielder of the New York Yankees, win their circuits' respective "Rookie of the Year" awards. For Mays, it is the first major honor in a Hall of Fame career. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1933: Reds Trade George Grantham to Giants for Glenn Spencer
item.description: On November 15, 1933, the Reds traded second baseman George Grantham to the New York Giants in exchange for pitcher Glenn Spencer.

item.title: 1929: Billy Nash, 64, Longtime Third Baseman for Phillies
item.description: Billy Nash, 64, prominent third baseman for the Richmond Virginians, Boston Beaneaters and Philadelphia Phillies from 1884 through 1898, who posted a .275 batting average with 60 home runs and 979 runs batted in for 1550 games, while scoring 100 runs four times and collecting 110 or more RBI two times, also leading the National League in putouts, double plays and fielding average four times each. Photo: Goodwin & Co., sponsor (Public domain).

item.title: 1916: Jack Farrell, 60, Center Fielder for 1874 Hartford Dark Blues
item.description: Jack Farrell 60, center fielder who hit .385 in three games with the 1874 Hartford Dark Blues of the National Association.
